copy.headline: 7 foods you're refrigerating that should be on the counter.
Tomatoes.
items: Cold destroys the enzymes that create flavor. Counter: up to 7 days once ripe.
Fridge turns them mealy and tasteless.
copy.citation: USDA Food Safety; UC Davis Postharvest Center

copy.headline: Bananas.
items: Refrigerating unripe bananas halts ripening permanently.
Leave them on the counter until yellow with spots.
Only refrigerate once fully ripe — then you get 4–5 more days (skin browns, flesh stays fine).

copy.headline: Potatoes.
items: Cold converts their starch to sugar — making them gritty and overly sweet when cooked. Cool, dark pantry: 3–5 weeks.

copy.headline: Onions.
items: Fridge moisture softens and molds them faster.
Once cut, then refrigerate — and use within 7–10 days.

copy.headline: Garlic.
items: A cool, dry spot with ventilation keeps whole bulbs fresh 3–6 months. Individual cloves: 3 weeks.

copy.headline: Avocados (unripe).
items: It yields to gentle pressure when ready.
Only refrigerate after ripe — never before.

copy.citation: USDA FoodData Central; UC Davis Postharvest Center; FDA Refrigerator & Freezer Storage Chart (2018); National Onion Association
